hero.title: Niger Military Unrest and Nepal Flood Disaster Dominate Global Headlines
hero.description: Military unrest in Niger's capital and the continuing humanitarian disaster in Nepal are among the major developing stories this morning, alongside the Iran–US conflict, Venezuela oil developments, China–US technology tensions and Nigeria's security crisis.

breaking: Niger capital Niamey faces serious military unrest
Nepal flood death toll reaches hundreds as thousands remain missing
Iran faces severe economic pressure as conflict with the US continues
China–US semiconductor tensions deepen over CXMT
US announces major new move involving Venezuela's oil sector

featured.title: Niger Capital Faces Serious Military Unrest
featured.content: Mutinous soldiers attacked strategic locations in Niamey, including the airport and presidential palace. Reuters reports that loyalist forces regained control of much of the capital, although the situation remained fluid. Claims describing a completed government overthrow should not be treated as confirmed without reliable official evidence.

articles.title: BREAKING: Niger Capital Faces Serious Military Unrest
articles.description: Mutinous soldiers attacked strategic locations in Niamey, including the airport and presidential palace. Reuters reports loyalist forces regained control of much of the capital, although the situation remained fluid and the airport remained contested at the time of reporting.

articles.title: Nepal Flood Disaster Death Toll Rises
articles.description: Nepal has resumed search-and-rescue operations following a devastating flood linked to a glacier collapse. Reuters reports at least 669 deaths in Nepal and seven in Tibet, while nearly 3,000 people remain missing across affected areas.

articles.title: Nepal Faces Billions in Reconstruction Costs
articles.description: Nepal is seeking international technical assistance as it confronts the aftermath of catastrophic flooding. Officials estimate reconstruction could cost between $4 billion and $5 billion.

articles.title: Iran Faces Growing Economic Pressure
articles.description: Iran is facing severe economic pressure as its conflict with the United States continues. Foreign trade has fallen, inflation has surged and sanctions are putting additional strain on the economy.

articles.title: China–US Semiconductor Rivalry Deepens
articles.description: Chinese memory-chip manufacturer CXMT has taken legal action against the US Department of Defense over its inclusion on a US list of companies considered linked to China's military.

articles.title: US Announces Major Venezuela Oil Move
articles.description: US President Donald Trump has announced a major new US role involving Venezuela's oil sector. The development could significantly affect US–Venezuela relations and regional energy markets.

articles.title: Washington Watches Niger Military Crisis
articles.description: The United States is closely watching developments in Niger following reports of military unrest in the capital. The situation remains developing and details continue to emerge.

articles.title: European Energy Security Remains Under Pressure
articles.description: European governments continue monitoring developments in the Middle East because disruption to oil and gas supplies could affect energy prices, inflation and economic activity across the region.

articles.title: Hormuz Remains Central to Global Energy Security
articles.description: The continuing Iran–US conflict keeps the Strait of Hormuz at the centre of international energy concerns. Any prolonged disruption to shipping could affect fuel and transportation costs worldwide.

articles.title: Nigeria's Kidnapping Crisis Remains a Major Concern
articles.description: Nigeria continues to face serious pressure from mass kidnappings. A security study cited by Reuters estimated that kidnappers collected almost $5.8 million in ransom payments from civilian abductions during the past year.

articles.title: Guinea-Bissau Holds Constitutional Referendum
articles.description: Voters in Guinea-Bissau are scheduled to vote on a proposed constitution that would expand presidential powers. The referendum is taking place after the country came under military leadership following last year's coup.

articles.title: Nigeria's Economic Outlook Remains Under Watch
articles.description: Nigeria's improved economic outlook continues to attract investor attention, although fiscal pressure, debt challenges, inflation and security concerns remain important risks.

articles.title: Global Markets Watch Middle East Energy Risks
articles.description: Investors remain focused on oil prices, inflation, interest rates and geopolitical risks as the Iran–US conflict continues to threaten energy and shipping routes.

articles.title: Venezuela Oil Developments Could Affect Energy Markets
articles.description: Washington's announced move involving Venezuela's oil sector could have wider consequences for regional energy relations and global crude markets.

articles.title: Energy Security Remains a Global Economic Risk
articles.description: Continued instability around major oil-producing regions is keeping energy security high on the international economic agenda. Further disruptions could affect fuel prices, inflation and transportation costs.

articles.title: CXMT Legal Fight Highlights China–US Chip Tensions
articles.description: CXMT's legal challenge against the US Department of Defense highlights the growing technology rivalry between Washington and Beijing over semiconductors and advanced computing.

articles.title: China Pushes Further Into Domestic Chip Production
articles.description: China continues expanding domestic semiconductor manufacturing as companies seek to strengthen local supply chains and reduce dependence on foreign technology.

articles.title: AI Investment Remains a Global Business Story
articles.description: Artificial intelligence continues attracting huge investment in chips, data centres and computing infrastructure as companies and investors assess the long-term returns of the AI boom.

morningSummary.title: MORNING SUMMARY
morningSummary.description: Security and natural disasters dominate the global headlines this morning. Niger's capital Niamey is facing serious military unrest, although the exact political outcome remains developing. Nepal continues a huge search-and-rescue operation following catastrophic flooding, with hundreds dead and thousands missing. Iran remains under severe economic pressure as its conflict with the United States continues. A major new US move involving Venezuela's oil sector could influence regional energy relations, while China–US semiconductor tensions continue to deepen. Nigeria's kidnapping crisis and Guinea-Bissau's constitutional referendum are also important African developments.

bigQuestion: In a world facing war, natural disasters and insecurity, should governments focus first on preventing crises or improving their ability to respond when disaster strikes?
quoteOfTheDay: You cannot control every storm around you, but you can choose the strength, wisdom and courage with which you face it.
